title: The one-letter meter
hookLine: ajai alai abhai abai: unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging (Jaap, ek achhari)
last: KHAL KHANDDAN — BREAK CRUELTY, ADORN EARTH.

lines: A SOUND WITH ITS OWN LETTER.
cards: Say ah. Just the sound, mouth open, nothing else. It's the sound at the doctor's office, the sound of relief when you sit down after a long day, the sound of surprise.
In Gurmukhi it has its own letter, airha, near the very start of the alphabet. Now put that sound at the front of almost every word in a stanza, and build the whole meter on it. Jaap Sahib has one.

teach.b: The meter is called ek achhari. Ek is one, achhar is a letter: the one-letter meter.
Sikh teachers explain the name in more than one way, but you can hear the plainest reason straight away: almost every word in these stanzas begins with the same letter, the a that means without.
The first line: ajai, alai, abhai, abai. Four words, four doors closing on four old fears.
Ajai: jai is victory, being conquered, so ajai is unconquerable. Nobody defeats the One. Alai: lai is dissolving, being destroyed, so alai is indestructible.
Abhai: bhai is fear, so abhai is fearless. Abai: bai is age, wearing down, so abai is ageless, unchanging. Listen to what's underneath.
Defeat, destruction, fear, decay: call them four shadows over a human life, losing, being wiped out, being afraid, getting old. And each is answered with a single short a.
After the long names, the Persian titles and the doubled words, the praise here gets very small and very fast.

Some reciters fly through these lines so quickly they sound like rain on a roof, as if the hymn has run out of room for anything but the essentials. And Jaap keeps coming back to one of these four in particular.
Tomorrow, the one in the middle: abhai.

how: Sikhs recite the ek achhari stanzas near the end of Jaap Sahib very quickly, and many know the line ajai, alai, abhai, abai by heart.

o: a line repeated once for each Guru
a hymn sung in one breath without stopping
a meter where almost every word starts with a

games.q: the one-letter meter — tap the pairs.

s: ek is one, achhar is a letter; nearly every word begins with the same a.
the one-letter stanzas are the slowest part of Jaap
they're among the fastest; reciters can sound like rain on a roof.

games.q: defeat, destruction, fear and decay hang over every human life. how does the ek achhari line answer them?
o: with a long explanation of each.
with four short words: ajai, alai, abhai, abai.
games.why: unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging: each shadow answered with a single small a, without.

practice: Say the four words slowly, with a breath after each: ajai, alai, abhai, abai. Then say them a little faster, the way they're recited, and feel the rhythm. Stop, and sit with the open sound of a, the one at the front of every word.

wordCard.voice: Ek achhari. The one-letter meter, where nearly every word begins with a: ajai, alai, abhai, abai — unconquerable, indestructible, fearless, unchanging.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: the first line of Jaap's ek achhari, each word opening with the same letter.

carryVoice: Your line: ajai, alai, abhai, abai. Four shadows, and four short answers to them. See you tomorrow.
